title: Ethiopian Tamarind Juice
community: Eastern and southern Ethiopia — the tamarind drink
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Tamarind Juice — tamarind pods soaked in warm water, kneaded to dissolve, strained, and sweetened with honey and a touch of cardamom. The refreshing sour drink of Ethiopia's lowland and eastern communities — intensely tart, naturally cooling.
longDesc: Tamarind juice is the cooling drink of Ethiopia's hot lowland areas — where temperatures are high and tartness is welcome, the tamarind pod dissolved in water produces a drink that is simultaneously refreshing and nutritious.
steps: If using pods: remove shells. Soak tamarind in warm water 10 minutes.
Knead tamarind to dissolve pulp. Strain out seeds and fibres.
If using paste: dissolve directly in warm water.
Add honey and cardamom. Stir well.
chefTips: Tamarind juice is intensely sour — adjust honey to taste.
Cold is essential — this is a refresher drink.
commonMistakes: Not straining thoroughly — seeds and fibres unpleasant.
cookingScience: Tamarind's primary acid is tartaric acid — rarer than citric or malic acid and producing a distinctive, deeper sourness. The tartaric acid content is also what makes tamarind an excellent digestive aid.
sustainabilityTips: Wild-harvested tamarind from Ethiopia's lowland forests.
servedWith: As a cooling drink in hot weather
At Ramadan iftar as a sweet-sour refresher
culturalNote: Tamarind juice is the drink of the Ethiopian lowlands — where the highland communities drink coffee and tella, the hot lowland areas of the Rift Valley and the east reach for tamarind to cool down.
